Content: WHY WE EXISIT: The best products Asia produces deserve to win. We have been a frustrated client and we refuse to repeat vendors flaws
WHAT WE OFFER: A design and engineering consultancy that treats a client's growth as a business problem, and builds exactly what that problem needs, for them and/or their customers.

WHO WE GO AFTER: Established Asian companies, ambitious and quality-minded, not chasing cheap, that want a partner to hit a named goal. Two shapes: (1) a healthy offline business but an online sales or marketing channel that badly underperforms or yet to exist; (2) a business with a particular challenge that demands deep engineering, frustrated by traditional process lag.

WHERE WE SIT: The empty space between studios that only reach a domestic audience and international agencies that can't build with real depth. We're neither niche players nor a team-rental, 'everything and nothing' shop. Pair that with AI-accelerated delivery and the space is ours.

HOW WE DELIVER: Consultants, not order-takers: we lead with the problem, and prove the solution with fast, working prototype, not endless back-and-forth discussions. An international team with a combination of deep engineering and AI-native knowhow, we measures success by speed, quality, value and judgement.

We build the software Asia's best companies should already have. It wins new customers at home or abroad, or runs your operation better. We show, not tell: a usable version in days, before any big commitment.

Operational: we get to the heart of how your business works, then build the system around the problem. Block: P1 Already know they have a problem
Content: Owner example: Jadegia. Situation: a validated prospect who already knows their site underperforms. Pitch approach: fix the underperforming site. Confidence: Strong (proven with client example).

Block: P2 Previous vendor attempts have failed
Content: Situation: burned by past vendors, trust must be rebuilt. Barrier: skepticism from prior bad delivery. Pitch approach: rebuild trust through proof, a working prototype. Confidence: Medium/Strong (prototype approach validated with Inkslap and Jadegia).

Block: P3 Doesn't sell online / no website
Content: Owner type: offline traditionalist. Barrier: doesn't perceive the pain, so won't pay. Pitch approach: reveal the hidden cost of being offline; prototype alone is insufficient, needs market-data / economics evidence. Confidence: Low/Medium (a hardware store prospect may validate).

Block: P4 Start-up founder, no proven business
Content: Owner type: non-technical founder, untested theoretical segment. Barrier: no proven business. Pitch approach: enable the non-technical founder to build; needs evidence beyond a prototype. Confidence: Weak (theoretical, untested market).

Block: P5 Sells online via intermediary platforms
Content: Owner type: marketplace-dependent business. Barrier: dependent on platforms, commission 20-35% as a hidden cost. Pitch approach: ownership vs. rental economics. Confidence: Weak (no evidence yet but a logical opportunity).
